rule: Owner, 2026-09-28: AURA is JEET-first but multi-company-ready. Every hardcoded business rule found while closing a gap is logged here and classified; nothing here is built yet.

candidates.rule: The business day is Dubai's: every 'today', due date and business date is computed in Asia/Dubai.
candidates.note: Right for JEET; a company or branch in another zone would get Dubai's day. Belongs to company/branch settings with effective dates. The non-UTC due-date behaviour stays recorded as unproven.

candidates.rule: An upload may be at most 25 MB.
candidates.where: FileInterceptor limits repeated 10 times across 6 API controllers (commissioning, crm-leads, pre-award-package, quality, site, tendering)
candidates.note: A company setting under a platform ceiling. Ten copies of one literal can already drift; one source is owed before it becomes configurable.

candidates.rule: Every upload is virus-scanned, and no verdict means no upload (fail-closed).
candidates.note: An administrator may not switch scanning off. The scanner host is deployment configuration, not company configuration.

candidates.rule: A handover that states no warranty period opens a 12-month AMC.
candidates.note: The default warranty / defects-liability period is a company (or contract) term.

candidates.rule: A customer invoice without a VAT rate is charged 5%.
candidates.note: Tax jurisdiction and rate by company, with effective dates. See VAT-BASIS-01 for the separate bid-inclusive / award-exclusive basis defect.

candidates.rule: Money is AED: the currency literal 'AED' appears in at least 26 non-test source files.
candidates.note: Base currency is company configuration; multi-currency is a separate decision, not implied.

candidates.rule: The System Administrator role holds every permission ('*'), business approvals included.
candidates.note: Conflicts with the owner's principle 'system administration ≠ business authority'. Removing it is a deliberate migration with a break-glass design, not a quiet edit.

candidates.rule: Who approves a quotation, in what order, above which amount.
candidates.note: Already a versioned company policy — the reference shape for Admin Center Level 1. The owner's default (TM → Commercial → Sales) stays a DRAFT until the Executive amount is decided.

candidates.rule: A purchase order's supplier is fixed once the order leaves draft.
candidates.note: Commitment integrity: a company may add approvals before issue, not reopen an issued commitment to another supplier.

candidates.rule: An IPC is valued as Σ certified quantity × the frozen awarded rate; the QS types quantities only.
candidates.note: Owner decision 2026-09-28. 'Configuration changes ≠ historical changes': the rate is the one frozen at award, whatever changes later.

candidates.rule: An inbound machine webhook (fleet telemetry) authenticates one tenant per deployment: one shared secret, one bound tenant.
candidates.note: Right for JEET-first. A second company needs its own credential bound to its own tenant, issued and rotated from company settings. The signature check itself is a platform invariant and stays fail-closed.

candidates.rule: The owner-decided holders of each authority act (SEC-01 D-01…D-13: payments, VAT, guarantees, engineering review, RFIs, variations, lifecycle, authority approvals, devices, documents, estimation) are the Standard Contractor default written into the role catalogue.
candidates.where: core/src/identity/standard-elv-roles.ts (the decision constants), pinned by apps/api/src/sec01-stage4.fitness.test.ts
candidates.note: Right for JEET. Another company will name different holders. Making this configurable means the fitness pin moves to the default policy, not that it goes away. The separation-of-duties rules that came with the decisions are platform invariants and are NOT to be made configurable: an author may not review or decide their own engineering item, a raiser may not answer their own RFI or decide their own variation, and a variation is decided only after submission.

candidates.rule: A submission to an authority is made as a controlled package (a transmittal that was sent) or through an authority portal (a stored receipt plus the portal reference).
candidates.note: That a submission never exists without evidence is a platform invariant. Which methods exist, and what evidence each needs, is company/authority configuration: a hand-delivered submission with a stamped acknowledgement, say. Adding a method today takes a code change and a migration to the check.

candidates.rule: A customer receipt must carry the date the money was received and a bank reference (transfer id or cheque number); a receipt with no reference cannot be recorded.
candidates.note: Right for a contractor paid by transfer and cheque. A company that takes cash receipts would need a method with its own evidence (a cash receipt number, say) rather than a blank reference. That a receipt is its own record and the paid amount is their sum is a platform invariant and is NOT to be made configurable.
